
| Instrument | Type | Tags |
|---|---|---|
| `inertia.page.duration` (s) | histogram | `inertia.response`, `inertia.partial` |
| `inertia.page.size` (By) | histogram | `inertia.response` |
| `inertia.ssr.duration` (s) | histogram | `inertia.ssr.outcome` |
| `inertia.ssr.queue.duration` (s) | histogram | |
| `inertia.ssr.active` | up-down counter | |
| `inertia.ssr.outcomes` | counter | `inertia.ssr.outcome`, `inertia.ssr.reason` |
| `inertia.ssr.response.size` (By) | histogram | |
| `inertia.ssr.circuit.state` | gauge | `inertia.ssr.endpoint` |
| `inertia.ssr.circuit.transitions` | counter | `inertia.ssr.endpoint`, `to` |
| `inertia.ssr.process.restarts` | counter | `cause` |
| `inertia.props.rescued` | counter | |

Tag values are bounded: no URLs, component names or user data. The `inertia.render` activity carries `inertia.component`; the `inertia.ssr` activity carries `inertia.ssr.endpoint`, `inertia.ssr.outcome` and `inertia.ssr.reason`. Nothing is recorded unless a listener is attached.

## 9. Response cache

A render depends only on the page JSON, so a page that many visitors see byte for byte the same can reuse its HTML:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Ssr.Cache.Duration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
    o.Ssr.Cache.StaleFor = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30);
    o.Ssr.Cache.MaxBytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
});

return Render("Pricing", props).WithSsrCache(TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
return Render("Pricing", props).WithSsrCache(TimeSpan.FromHours(1), staleFor: TimeSpan.FromDays(1));
```

The key is the SHA-256 of the page JSON (component, props, url, version and the rest), so a new deploy or different props never reuse a stale render. Pages with per-user props make one entry per user; cache the pages that are shared. A hit is counted as `inertia.ssr.outcomes{inertia.ssr.outcome=rendered, inertia.ssr.reason=cache}` and bypasses the render slots and circuit breakers. Nothing is cached while the Vite dev server renders.

Concurrent misses for the same page share one fill per app instance. Waiting counts against `Ssr.Timeout`; cancelling a waiting request does not cancel the request filling the entry.

With `StaleFor`, a render past its `Duration` is still served and rendered again after the response, like stale props. `IInertiaCache.ClearSsrAsync()` removes every render.

---

# Vite

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/vite-integration

> Manifest tags, the dev-server hot file, asset base URLs, prefetching and CSP nonces.

`ViteAssets` (a singleton, also usable directly as `vite.RenderTags(httpContext, "resources/js/app.tsx")`) renders the tags for the `@vite(...)` token and the `<vite />` tag helper.

## Production

In production Inertia.Net reads `wwwroot/build/.vite/manifest.json` (falling back to `wwwroot/build/manifest.json` for older Vite). It parses the manifest once and pre-renders the tags to UTF-8. For each entry it emits, in order:

1. `<link rel="stylesheet">` for the entry's CSS and the CSS of its static imports, recursively and deduplicated;
2. `<script type="module" src="...">` for the entry file;
3. `<link rel="modulepreload">` for each static import.

URLs are `{PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}/{file}` so apps under a path base work, or `{AssetBaseUrl}/{file}`. An entry missing from the manifest throws with the list of available entries. A missing manifest throws with the paths it looked in.

## Development

While the dev server runs, the tags are `@vite/client` and the entry from the dev server origin, plus the React Refresh preamble for `@viteReactRefresh`. The dev server counts as running when:

- `o.Vite.DevServerUrl` is set (always, in any environment), or
- the environment is Development and the hot file (`wwwroot/hot` by default) exists and contains the origin.

The hot file is written by your Vite config. The `@inertiajs/vite` plugin does not write one, so the samples include a small plugin that does.

<Callout type="warning" title="base must differ between dev and build">
Built assets are served from `/build/`, so the Vite `base` is `/build/` for a build. The dev server must serve from the root because Inertia.Net emits `{origin}/@vite/client` and `{origin}/{entry}`. Use `base: command === 'build' ? '/build/' : '/'`.
</Callout>

## Options

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Vite.PublicDirectory = "wwwroot";                        // default
    o.Vite.BuildDirectory = "build";                           // default
    o.Vite.ManifestPath = null;                                // default wwwroot/build/.vite/manifest.json
    o.Vite.HotFilePath = null;                                 // default wwwroot/hot
    o.Vite.DevServerUrl = builder.Environment.IsDevelopment() ? "http://localhost:5173" : null;
    o.Vite.AssetBaseUrl = "https://cdn.example.com/build";     // serve built assets from a CDN
});
```

Only plain http(s) origins without quotes or markup are accepted from the hot file or `DevServerUrl`, because the origin is echoed into a script.

With `AssetBaseUrl` set, Vite's own `base` must match so lazily imported chunks resolve against the CDN too:

```ts
base: 'https://cdn.example.com/build/'
```

## Prefetching

Page components resolved with lazy `import.meta.glob` are separate chunks that the browser downloads only when a page needs them. `o.Vite.Prefetch` downloads them after the page loads, at low priority, so the next navigation does not wait:

```csharp
o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Waterfall;   // PrefetchConcurrency (default 3) at a time
o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Aggressive;  // all at once
```

The tags get one small inline script with the list of chunks the entries can import later (dynamic imports, then their static imports and CSS), minus those already loaded. It is rendered once per entry set.

## Content Security Policy

With a nonce-based CSP, set `o.CspNonce` to the request's nonce. Every script and stylesheet tag Inertia.Net writes then carries it: the page `<script data-page>`, the Vite tags, the React refresh preamble and the prefetch script (whose links get it too).

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.CspNonce = ctx => ctx.Items["csp-nonce"] as string);

app.Use((ctx, next) =>
{
    var nonce = Convert.ToBase64String(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16));
    ctx.Items["csp-nonce"] = nonce;
    ctx.Response.Headers.ContentSecurityPolicy =
        $"script-src 'nonce-{nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'";
    return next(ctx);
});
```

The nonce must be base64 or base64url; anything else throws. Cached tags are split where the nonce goes, so a nonce costs one copy of the tag bytes per request and no re-rendering.

<Callout type="tip" title="Static assets">
Use `app.UseStaticFiles()` with a long `Cache-Control` for `/build/assets`, or `app.MapStaticAssets()` when the client is built before `dotnet publish`. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying).
</Callout>

---

# Asset versioning

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/asset-versioning

> Tell the client when its JavaScript and CSS are stale, and reload once when they are.

The asset version tells the client when its assets are stale. The server resolves it in this order:

1. `InertiaOptions.VersionResolver(HttpContext)`, when it returns non-null;
2. else `InertiaOptions.Version`;
3. else a hash of the Vite manifest (the first 16 bytes of its SHA-256, in hex), computed once and recomputed in Development when the file changes;
4. else `""`.

```csharp
o.Version = typeof(Program).Assembly.GetName().Version!.ToString();       // or a build id
o.VersionResolver = ctx => ctx.Request.Headers["X-Tenant"].ToString();   // per request
```

## How the client checks it

When an Inertia **GET** carries a different `X-Inertia-Version`, the server answers `409` with `X-Inertia-Location` (the absolute request URL) and `X-Inertia-Version`, and the client performs a full page reload.

The check runs **before your handler**, so no work is wasted rendering a page that will be thrown away. Other methods never get this `409`.

```text
GET /users
X-Inertia: true
X-Inertia-Version: old

409 Conflict
X-Inertia-Location: https://example.com/users
X-Inertia-Version: new
```

## Choosing a version

- **Vite manifest hash (default).** Nothing to configure. A new build changes the manifest and the version.
- **Assembly version or build id.** Good when the client build is not tied to the manifest, or when several apps share assets.
- **Per-request version.** Useful for multi-tenant apps with different frontend builds per tenant.

<Callout type="danger" title="Never generate a new version on every request">
A `VersionResolver` that returns a random value on every call makes the client reload forever. Different instances behind a load balancer must serve the same build, or the client will bounce between versions.
</Callout>

## Path base

The version check and `X-Inertia-Location` use the request URL. Behind a path base or reverse proxy, configure forwarded headers so the scheme and host match the browser's URL. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying).

---

# CSRF protection

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/csrf-and-antiforgery

> Protect forms with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.

The Inertia client reads the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and sends its value as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on every request. `UseInertiaAntiforgery()` issues that cookie and validates it, so one call protects every form.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAntiforgery(o => o.HeaderName = InertiaHeaders.XsrfToken);   // "X-XSRF-TOKEN"

app.UseAuthentication();                 // if the app signs users in: the token is bound to the signed-in user
app.UseInertia();
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery();
```

## What it does

- **Issue.** Page loads (GET/HEAD requests that are Inertia requests or accept `text/html`) get the request token in a script-readable, essential cookie (`HttpOnly` off, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, `Secure` per `SecurePolicy`). Essential means a cookie-consent policy does not withhold it.
- **Validate.** Every unsafe request (anything but GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE), with a JSON or a form body, Inertia or not, is checked with `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync`. A plain cross-site HTML form post is rejected as well as a forged XHR. It also sets the antiforgery feature, so form-binding endpoints work without `app.UseAntiforgery()`.
- **Reject.** A missing or wrong token gets **`419`** (page expired, as in Laravel); the handler does not run.
- **Opt out** per endpoint with `.DisableAntiforgery()` (webhooks, test hooks), or for whole areas with `ShouldValidate`.

## Options

```csharp
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(o =>
{
    o.CookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN";                                  // default
    o.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always;                   // default SameAsRequest
    o.ShouldValidate = ctx => !ctx.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/api");
    o.OnRejected = (ctx, error) => Back().WithFlash("error", "The page expired, please try again.");
});
```

`OnRejected` runs after `UseInertia()`; returning `Back()` gives the tab a fresh token and a message instead of the client's error dialog.

## Lazy refresh

By default every page load issues a fresh token, and antiforgery marks that response `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store` (which also keeps the page out of the browser's back/forward cache).

`o.CookieRefresh = XsrfCookieRefresh.Lazy` keeps a token that still validates. Such responses get no `Set-Cookie` and stay cacheable, and a token issued before a sign-in or sign-out is replaced on the next page load.

Validating costs about what issuing does, so the gain is in the responses, not in CPU. Set your own `Cache-Control` on pages with private data.

<Callout type="info" title="Session changes">
A session that expires or a sign-in that changes the user invalidates the token in an open tab; the next page load issues a new one. Returning `Back()` from `OnRejected` gives that tab a fresh token and a message.
</Callout>

## MVC and FastEndpoints

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` covers controllers too. `[AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken]` as a global filter still works, but is not needed. FastEndpoints is covered by the middleware; FastEndpoints' own `EnableAntiforgery()` is not needed for Inertia forms.

## Issue only

`UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN")` (the 1.0 API) only writes the cookie. You then validate with `app.UseAntiforgery()` (form bodies only) and your own check for JSON bodies (`await antiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context)`). Prefer `UseInertiaAntiforgery()`.

## Troubleshooting 419

- Was the page loaded through the middleware? It sets the cookie.
- Does the cookie reach the browser? `Secure` cookies are dropped on plain HTTP; behind a TLS-terminating proxy, configure forwarded headers or set `CookieSecurePolicy.Always`.
- Do all instances share the Data Protection key ring?
- Does `UseAuthentication()` run before the antiforgery middleware?
- Did a sign-in or sign-out change the token? Reload the page, or use `OnRejected`.

See [Deploying](/docs/deploying) for proxy and multi-instance settings.

---

# Deploying behind a proxy

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/deploying

> Forwarded headers, secure cookies, compression, asset caching and multi-instance state.

Behind a load balancer or reverse proxy that terminates TLS, Kestrel sees plain HTTP unless the scheme is forwarded. Without it, the state and `XSRF-TOKEN` cookies are not marked `Secure`, and the version-mismatch `409` sends an `http://` `X-Inertia-Location`.

## Forwarded headers

```csharp
builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(o =>
{
    o.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    // o.KnownProxies / o.KnownNetworks: list your proxy, or headers from anyone else are ignored
});

app.UseForwardedHeaders();               // first
app.UseInertia();
```

When the scheme cannot be forwarded, force the cookies:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.State.CookieSecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always);
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(o => o.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always);
```

## Multi-instance state

On several instances, share the Data Protection key ring so the state cookie and antiforgery tokens can be read by every instance:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDataProtection()
    .PersistKeysToFileSystem(new DirectoryInfo("/var/keys"))
    .SetApplicationName("MyApp");
```

Using the session store? Sessions must be shared too (for example Redis). The default cookie store only needs shared Data Protection keys.

Keep the SSR server on loopback on each instance. See [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering).

## Compression

Page JSON and HTML compress five to ten times. Compress at the proxy, or in the app:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddResponseCompression();
app.UseResponseCompression();                // before UseStaticFiles and UseInertia
```

Over HTTPS the middleware compresses only with `o.EnableForHttps = true`. Review BREACH for your pages first: Inertia.Net keeps the antiforgery token in a cookie, not in the body, but a page that reflects request input next to a secret is still exposed.

## Asset caching

Vite puts a content hash in every built file name, so files under `build/assets` can be cached for good:

```csharp
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    OnPrepareResponse = c =>
    {
        if (c.Context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/build/assets"))
        {
            c.Context.Response.Headers.CacheControl = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }
    },
});
```

`app.MapStaticAssets()` does the same with build-time Brotli when the client is built before `dotnet publish`, so the files are in `wwwroot` when the static web assets manifest is generated.

## Path base

Use `app.UsePathBase("/app")` before `UseInertia()`. The page `url`, Vite URLs and `Back()` include the path base. If a proxy rewrites paths, set `o.UrlResolver` to return the browser-visible URL.

## Health and readiness

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddInertiaSsr();
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The SSR health check is covered in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering#7-health-check).

## Deployment checklist

- [ ] `npm run build` runs before `dotnet publish`, or `wwwroot/build` is copied into the publish output.
- [ ] `app.html` is copied to the publish output.
- [ ] Forwarded headers are configured, or cookies are forced secure.
- [ ] Data Protection keys are shared between instances.
- [ ] Static assets under `/build/assets` are cached as immutable.
- [ ] Response compression is enabled at the proxy or in the app.
- [ ] SSR listens on loopback and its bundle is deployed when SSR is enabled.
- [ ] The client build and server build are the same version, so `X-Inertia-Version` converges.

---

# Native AOT

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/native-aot

> Publish a Native AOT Inertia.Net app with source-generated JSON metadata.

`Inertia.Net` and `Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints` are annotated `IsAotCompatible`. A real app is published with Native AOT in CI (`tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke`) with zero trim and AOT warnings allowed. The library never reflects over your props: values are written with `JsonTypeInfo` from your `JsonSerializerContext`.

## 1. Register a JSON context

Register every prop type and chain the context into the HTTP JSON options:

```csharp
builder.Services.ConfigureHttpJsonOptions(o =>
    o.SerializerOptions.TypeInfoResolverChain.Insert(0, AppJsonContext.Default));

[JsonSerializable(typeof(UsersPage))]               // typed page props
[JsonSerializable(typeof(UserDto))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<UserDto>))]           // closed collection types you return
[JsonSerializable(typeof(UserDto[]))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Stats))]                   // the T of Defer(() => new Stats(...)) and friends
internal sealed partial class AppJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
```

Register the type that each loader returns and each plain value you place in `InertiaProps`, plus flash values that are not plain strings or numbers. The library's own context already covers `string`, `bool`, `int`, `long`, `double`, `decimal`, `float`, `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `TimeSpan`, `JsonElement`, `string[]`, `int[]`, `List<string>`, `Dictionary<string, string>`, `Dictionary<string, string[]>`, `InertiaProps` and `Dictionary<string, object>`.

Members of type `InertiaProp` are accepted by the source generator without any attribute.

## 2. Make validation models public

The .NET 10 `AddValidation()` source generator skips internal types, and validation then silently does nothing. Only one `AddValidation()` call site per project is allowed.

## 3. Add ProblemDetails

```csharp
builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
```

The non-Inertia `400` validation problem needs the `ProblemDetails` JSON metadata, or it cannot be serialized without reflection.

## 4. Avoid anonymous types

Anonymous types do not work as props or flash values under AOT. Use `InertiaProps`, records or classes registered in the context.

## 5. Copy content files

`app.html` and the Vite manifest are read from disk at runtime. Copy them to the publish directory, and set the content root to the binary's directory when it may run from elsewhere:

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder(new WebApplicationOptions
{
    Args = args,
    ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory,
});
```

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>
  <JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>false</JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault>
</PropertyGroup>
<ItemGroup>
  <Content Include="app.html" CopyToPublishDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
</ItemGroup>
```

## 6. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints

MVC is not AOT compatible (neither is MVC itself), so `Inertia.Net.Mvc` is not either. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints.

## 7. FastEndpoints source generation

```csharp
builder.Services.AddFastEndpoints(new[] { DiscoveredTypes.All });
```

`DiscoveredTypes` is generated by the `FastEndpoints.Generator` package, in the namespace named after the assembly. See `samples/FastEndpoints.Svelte`.

## 8. Trim HTTP/3

The SSR client never uses HTTP/3, so it can be trimmed out:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Net.SocketsHttpHandler.Http3Support" Value="false" Trim="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Cached props, the SSR cache, nonces, prefetching, `MapInertia` and the DevTools recorder are all AOT safe and covered by the smoke test.

<Callout type="tip" title="Catch missing registrations early">
Set `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` in regular builds too. A missing `JsonSerializable` registration then fails in tests instead of only in the AOT publish.
</Callout>

The reference app is `tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke/Program.cs`. Run it end to end with `bash eng/aot-smoke.sh` on Linux with clang and zlib installed.

---

# Performance

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/performance

> Memory and hosting guidance, payload limits and the design choices behind the adapter.

Benchmarks cover page rendering, partial reloads, deferred props, SSR, caching and state storage. These controlled microbenchmarks are not production throughput estimates.

## Memory and hosting

The useful planning number is not a microbenchmark; it is how much memory the whole process needs at rest and under load. These are reference points measured on Linux x64 after the first request, not guarantees:

| App shape | RSS at rest | Plan for |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inertia.Net JIT app, no database (`samples/MinimalApi.React`) | about 90 MB | 256–512 MB |
| Inertia.Net Native AOT app (`tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke`) | about 42 MB | 128–256 MB |
| Small JIT todo: Minimal API + EF Core + SQLite + cookie auth | roughly 120–180 MB | 256–512 MB |
| Small Native AOT todo: source-generated JSON + SQLite | roughly 45–70 MB | 128–256 MB |
| Add managed Bun SSR | +30–60 MB for the Bun process | add 128 MB headroom |

The two Inertia.Net baseline rows were measured from this repository on Linux x64; the todo rows are planning ranges, not benchmark claims. The JIT todo range includes the runtime, EF Core, SQLite, authentication and a small working set. PostgreSQL or MongoDB, image processing and a large cache move it upward; measure your own app under realistic concurrency. Native AOT removes most JIT and reflection overhead, but it does not make EF Core or a database free.

For containers:

- Set a memory limit rather than relying on the host.
- Leave headroom for the GC, the OS page cache and request bursts.
- Expect SSR to add a second process. If the Bun renderer is optional, `SsrMode.Preferred` lets the app fall back to client rendering when it is unavailable.
- Profile with real page sizes. A dashboard with deferred props and a paginated feed behaves very differently from a page that serializes every row.

The benchmark project still has the throughput and allocation probes:

```sh
dotnet run -c Release --project tests/Inertia.Net.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'
```

Targeted probes: `--render-probe`, `--ssr-probe`, `--mvc-probe`, `--payload-probe` and `--cache-probe`.

## Payload size

The page JSON is fully buffered before the first byte is sent, so a failing loader never produces a half-written `200`. Each concurrent request therefore holds its whole page in memory (pooled, and sized from the component's recent pages).

Keep pages well under a megabyte:

- paginate with [`Scroll`](/docs/infinite-scroll)
- defer slow data with [`Defer`](/docs/deferred-props)
- load on demand with [`Optional`](/docs/props#the-prop-factories)
- use a [partial reload](/docs/partial-reloads) for refresh buttons and filters

`Ssr.MaxPageBytes` keeps larger pages off the SSR server and `Ssr.MaxResponseBytes` bounds its answer; neither limits the props.

## Design notes

- **Single pass.** One recursive walk filters props, runs loaders, writes JSON to a `Utf8JsonWriter` and collects the metadata. There is no intermediate object tree.
- **Pooled buffers.** The page is written to a pooled `IBufferWriter<byte>`, and the path tracker is a pooled `char[]`. A path becomes a string only when metadata needs it.
- **Version check before the handler.** A stale client costs one header comparison and a `409`.
- **No per-request mutable singletons.** Per-request state lives in an `InertiaFeature` on `HttpContext.Features`, so concurrent requests cannot leak history or flash settings into one another.
- **Plain DTOs take the fast path.** A POCO, list or typed dictionary is walked only when its type can hold `InertiaProp` values (`InertiaProp`, `object` or dictionary members/elements; cached per type). Everything else is one `Serialize` call.
- **UTF-8 throughout.** SSR output and the MVC tag helpers write UTF-8 bytes; nothing large is materialized as a .NET string.
- **Cached assets.** The Vite manifest is parsed once, the root template is parsed once into pre-encoded UTF-8 segments, and the production tags are pre-rendered per entry set and path base. The version is a precomputed string compared ordinally. A missing manifest, template or SSR bundle is re-checked at most once per second.
- **Sync loaders stay sync.** `Func<T>` loaders are not wrapped in closures.

Most per-request allocation in a real handler is the props you build, not the render.

---

# Configuration

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/configuration

> InertiaOptions, Vite, SSR, props, state and the middleware and result API.

All configuration is passed to `AddInertia`. Options marked “Development only” do nothing in other environments.

## `AddInertia(o => ...)`: `InertiaOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RootView` | `"app.html"` | Root template relative to the content root (a Razor view name with `UseRazorRootView`). Paths outside the content root are refused. |
| `RootElementId` | `"app"` | Id of the root element and the `data-page` script. |
| `Version` | `null` | Asset version. `null` means the Vite manifest hash, or `""` without one. |
| `VersionResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>` per-request version; wins over `Version` when non-null. |
| `EncryptHistory` | `false` | Encrypt browser history state of every page. |
| `WithAllErrors` | `false` | Send every validation message per field instead of the first. |
| `PreserveBigIntegers` | `false` | Emit integers beyond ±(2^53−1) as `{"$bigint":"..."}`. |
| `ExposeSharedPropKeys` | `true` | List top-level shared keys in `sharedProps`. |
| `CspNonce` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>`: the request's CSP nonce. |
| `ConvertExternalRedirects` | `true` | Turn an Inertia redirect to another origin into `409` + `X-Inertia-Location`. |
| `UrlResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string>`: the page `url`. |
| `Pages.Directory` / `Pages.Extensions` | `null` / `.tsx .jsx .ts .js .vue .svelte` | Development check that a rendered component has a page file. |
| `TypeScript.OutputPath`, `.Page<T>(component)`, `.SharedProps<T>()`, `.FlashData<T>()` | `null` | TypeScript declarations, written in Development. |
| `Share(key, value)` / `Share(key, Func<HttpContext, object?>)` | none | Shared props. |

## `o.Vite`: `ViteOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PublicDirectory` | `"wwwroot"` | Web root containing the build directory and hot file. |
| `BuildDirectory` | `"build"` | Vite output directory under `PublicDirectory`; also the URL prefix. |
| `ManifestPath` | `null` | Manifest path relative to the content root. `null` = `{PublicDirectory}/{BuildDirectory}/.vite/manifest.json`, then `manifest.json`. |
| `HotFilePath` | `null` | Hot file relative to the content root. `null` = `{PublicDirectory}/hot`. Read in Development only. |
| `DevServerUrl` | `null` | Dev server origin, e.g. `http://localhost:5173`. When set, dev tags always render. |
| `AssetBaseUrl` | `null` | Replaces `{PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}` as the URL prefix of built assets. |
| `Prefetch` | `None` | `Waterfall` or `Aggressive`: prefetch code-split chunks after load. |
| `PrefetchConcurrency` | `3` | Chunks `Waterfall` downloads at a time. |

## `o.Ssr`: `SsrOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Mode` | `Disabled` | `Disabled`, `Preferred` or `Required`. `Disabled` cannot be overridden per response. |
| `Urls` | empty (`http://127.0.0.1:13714`) | SSR server base URLs. Not used with `UseNodeProcess()`. |
| `Timeout` | `5 s` | Total deadline per render. `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` disables it. |
| `MaxResponseBytes` | `16 MiB` | Limit on actual response bytes, including errors and chunked responses. |
| `MaxPageBytes` | `2 MiB` | Pages whose JSON is larger render on the client without a call. |
| `BundlePath` | `null` | Skip SSR while this file is missing, unless the Vite dev server runs. |
| `ExcludePaths` | empty | Request paths never rendered on the server (exact, or a trailing `*` for a prefix). |
| `Concurrency.MaxActive` | `8` | Renders in flight per server from this app instance; `0` for no limit. |
| `Concurrency.MaxQueued` | `32` | Renders waiting for a slot per server. |
| `Concurrency.QueueTimeout` | `250 ms` | How long a render waits for a slot. |
| `CircuitBreaker.Enabled` | `true` | Pause servers that keep failing. |
| `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` | `5` | Consecutive failures that open a server's circuit. |
| `CircuitBreaker.BreakDuration` | `10 s` | How long an open circuit skips the server before one probe. |
| `Cache.Duration` | `Zero` (off) | Reuse a render for this long when the page JSON is the same. |
| `Cache.StaleFor` | `Zero` | Serve stale while re-rendering. |
| `Cache.MaxBytes` | `64 MiB` | Size of the default store's render cache. |
| `UseNodeProcess(configure?)` | off | Start and supervise Node SSR processes (sets `Mode = Preferred` when `Disabled`). |

Per response: `Render(...).WithSsr(SsrMode)` and `.WithoutSsr()`. The full SSR options are in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering).

## `o.Props`: `InertiaPropsOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MaxConcurrency` | `4` | Loaders marked `.Parallel()` that run at once per render. Must be positive. |

## `o.State`: `InertiaStateOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CookieName` | `".Inertia.State"` | Cookie name (cookie store) or session key (session store). |
| `CookieSecurePolicy` | `SameAsRequest` | When the state cookie is `Secure`. |
| `UseSession()` | off | Use `ISession` instead of the encrypted cookie. |
| `AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseTempDataStateStore())` | off | Use MVC TempData. Inertia.Net.Mvc package. |

## Middleware and endpoint API

| API | Description |
|---|---|
| `services.AddInertia(configure?)` | Registers services and options. |
| `app.UseInertia()` | The protocol middleware. Before the endpoints; after `UseSession()` when used. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(configure?)` | Issues the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and validates unsafe requests (`419` on failure). |
| `app.MapInertia(pattern, component, props?)` | GET and HEAD endpoint that renders the component. |
| `services.AddInertiaDevTools(configure?)` / `app.MapInertiaDevTools()` | DevTools recorder and read API. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN")` | Only writes the token cookie; validation is up to you. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaValidation()` | Minimal API: validation failures redirect back with errors. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaPrecognition()` | Minimal API: `WithInertiaValidation()` plus Precognition. |
| `healthChecks.AddInertiaSsr(...)` | SSR health check from the gateway's state. |
| `mvc.AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseRazorRootView("App"))` | MVC filter, optional Razor root view and component resolver. |
| `config.UseInertia(configure?)` | FastEndpoints: validation redirect and Precognition. |
| `Render(component, props?)` | `InertiaResult`: `.WithStatusCode`, `.WithRootView`, `.WithViewData`, `.WithSsr`, `.WithoutSsr`, `.WithSsrCache`. |
| `Location(url)` | `InertiaLocationResult`. |
| `Back(fallback = "~/")` | `InertiaBackResult`: `.WithErrors`, `.WithFlash`. |
| `httpContext.Inertia()` | `InertiaFeature`: `Share`, `Flash`, `WithErrors`, `ClearHistory`, `EncryptHistory`, `PreserveFragment`. |
| `Send.InertiaAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaLocationAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaBackAsync(...)` | FastEndpoints `Send` extensions. |

## Extension points

`IInertiaRootView`, `IInertiaStateStore`, `ViteAssets`, `InertiaRequest` (parsed headers), `InertiaHeaders` (header name constants), `InertiaSsrException`, `InertiaSsr.HttpClientName` (the SSR HTTP client) and `InertiaDiagnostics` (meter and activity source names).

---

# TypeScript types

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/typescript

> Generate declarations for page props, shared props and flash data from your .NET contracts.

Inertia.Net can write TypeScript declarations for typed page props, shared props and flash data. They follow the app's JSON contracts (the HTTP JSON options and their source-generated contexts), so names, nullability and enum values match the page JSON.

## Configure generation

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.TypeScript.OutputPath = "ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts";   // written in Development, only when it changed
    o.TypeScript.Page<UsersPage>("Users/Index").Page<HomePage>("Home");
    o.TypeScript.FlashData<Flash>();                             // optional; SharedProps<T>() too
});

public sealed record UsersPage(
    List<User> Users,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(UserStats))] InertiaProp Stats);
```

The file is written when the app starts in Development, and only when its content changed. Commit it so `tsc` passes in CI without running the app.

```ts
// ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts (excerpt)
export interface InertiaPages {
  'Users/Index': UsersPage
  Home: HomePage
}
export interface UsersPage {
  users: User[]
  stats?: UserStats
}
declare module '@inertiajs/core' {
  export interface InertiaConfig {
    sharedPageProps: SharedProps
    flashDataType: FlashData
    errorValueType: string
  }
}
```

```tsx
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'

export default function Index({ users, stats }: InertiaPages['Users/Index']) {
  // ...
}
```

## Shared props

Shared props are inferred from the values passed to `o.Share(...)`; dot keys nest. Factories and per-request shares are typed as `unknown`. `o.TypeScript.SharedProps<T>()` replaces the inference with an explicit type. The `InertiaConfig` augmentation types `usePage().props` and `flash`.

## Prop members

An `InertiaProp` member is optional (it can be deferred, optional or rescued) and `unknown`, unless `[InertiaPropType(typeof(T))]` names its value type.

## Mapping

| .NET | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `int`, `long`, `double`, `decimal`, `float` | `number` (`number \| bigint` for 64-bit and larger with `PreserveBigIntegers`) |
| `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Guid`, `byte[]` | `string` |
| enum | union of JSON values (string names with a string enum converter) |
| dictionary | `Record<string, T>` |
| polymorphic type | union tagged with its discriminator |
| nullable member | `T \| null` |

Types missing from the JSON metadata (under Native AOT, register them in your context) are `unknown`, with a warning in the log.

Number handling follows member settings, then type settings, then the global JSON options. Custom converter output is typed as `unknown` with a warning when its shape cannot be inferred.

<Callout type="warning" title="Keep the HTTP and MVC naming policies aligned">
Props are written with the HTTP `JsonOptions`. MVC error keys use the MVC `JsonOptions`. If the two naming policies differ, generated prop names and validation error keys will not match.
</Callout>

---

# Testing

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/testing

> Fluent assertions over Inertia responses and helpers for partial reloads and deferred props.

`Inertia.Net.Testing` has Laravel-style fluent assertions over Inertia responses and `HttpClient` helpers. It parses both JSON responses (`X-Inertia: true`) and the first-visit HTML `<script data-page>`, and decodes `$bigint` values. Failures throw `InertiaAssertionException` with a readable message, so it works with any test framework.

```csharp
using Inertia.Net.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;

public class UsersTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory) : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    // Keeps cookies (flash, errors) and does not follow redirects, so a test can assert the 303 itself.
    private readonly HttpClient _client = factory.CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions
    {
        AllowAutoRedirect = false,
    });

    [Fact]
    public async Task Index_lists_users()
    {
        using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users");   // sends X-Inertia, X-Requested-With

        await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
            .Component("Users/Index")
            .Url("/users")
            .Has("users", 3, first => first.Where("name", "Ann").WhereType("id", "integer").Etc())
            .Where("filters.search", "")
            .Missing("secret")
            .HasFlash("toast", "Welcome"));
    }
}
```

Add `public partial class Program;` to your app when it uses top-level statements.

## Request helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `InertiaGetAsync(url, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia GET |
| `InertiaRequestAsync(method, url, content?, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia request with any method |
| `GetInertiaPageAsync()` | Parses the response into an `InertiaPage` |
| `AssertInertiaAsync(assert)` | Parses, runs the assertions and returns the page |

## Page assertions

`Component`, `Url`, `Version`, `HasFlash(key)`, `HasFlash(key, value)`, `MissingFlash(key)`, `HasDeferred(path)` and `HasDeferred(group, path)`.

## Prop assertions

On props and nested scopes (dot paths and array indexes allowed):

`Has(key)`, `Has(key, count)`, `Has(key, scope)`, `Has(key, count, firstItemScope)`, `HasAll`, `HasAny`, `Missing`, `MissingAll`, `Where(key, value)`, `Where(key, predicate)`, `WhereNot`, `WhereNull`, `WhereNotNull`, `WhereType(key, "string|null")`, `WhereAllType`, `WhereContains(key, ...)`, `Count`, `CountBetween`, `Each(scope)`, `First(scope)` and `Dump()`.

**Strict interaction tracking.** Like Laravel, a nested scope fails when it contains properties you did not assert, unless you end it with `Etc()`. The root scope is not checked automatically: call `.Interacted()` at the end to enforce that every top-level prop was asserted.

## Partial reloads and deferred props

`InertiaPage` replays the request with the right headers:

```csharp
var page = await (await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

new AssertableInertia(page).HasDeferred("sidebar", "stats").Missing("stats");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(_client, "sidebar");     // all groups when none are named
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats");

var only = await page.ReloadOnlyAsync(_client, "users");
var except = await page.ReloadExceptAsync(_client, "users");
```

`ReloadOnlyAsync` asserts that `"users"` is in the result; `ReloadExceptAsync` asserts that it is missing.

## InertiaPage members

`Props`, `Raw`, `Prop(path)`, `HasProp(path)`, `PropBigInteger(path)`, `DeferredProps`, `MergeProps`, `PrependProps`, `DeepMergeProps`, `MatchPropsOn`, `RescuedProps`, `SharedProps`, `ScrollProps`, `OnceProps`, `Flash`, `EncryptHistory`, `ClearHistory`, `PreserveFragment`, `PreserveBigIntegers`.

<Callout type="tip" title="Cookies and redirects">
Flash and errors travel in a cookie across the redirect, so use a client that keeps cookies. Disable `AllowAutoRedirect` to assert the redirect itself, then follow it with a second `InertiaGetAsync` to read the flash or errors.
</Callout>

---

# DevTools

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/devtools

> Record visits for the Inertia DevTools extension and catch missing page components during development.

The [Inertia DevTools](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/advanced/devtools) browser extension shows every visit, its props, headers and page state. Inertia.Net implements the server protocol.

## Enable DevTools

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaDevTools();   // records in Development only
app.UseInertia();
app.MapInertiaDevTools();                // GET /_inertia/devtools/entries/{id} and /entries
```

Each request through `UseInertia()` gets an `X-Inertia-Devtools-Id` and an entry in memory (per browser tab, at most `MaxEntriesPerTab` and `MaxEntries`, for `MaxAge`): request type, timings, headers, bodies, the page object and its props metadata.

The first page carries the discovery tag the extension reads. Values of names containing `password`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `api_key` are replaced with `[REDACTED]` in props, bodies and headers. Add names with `RedactedKeys`. Nothing leaves the app.

Sensitive query parameters are also redacted in recorded request/page URLs, redirects and URL headers; actual application URLs are unchanged. Malformed JSON bodies are omitted. Only eligible Inertia text bodies with a known length up to `MaxBodyBytes` are buffered; unknown-length nonseekable bodies are omitted as streamed, so recording does not spool bulk requests to disk.

Outside Development nothing is recorded unless `Enabled = true`, and the read API answers only requests that `Authorize` accepts (`404` otherwise). With `Pages.Directory` set, entries link the component to its file.

## Page component check

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Pages.Directory = "ClientApp/pages";   // Development only
    o.Pages.Extensions = [".tsx", ".vue"];   // optional
});
```

In Development, `Render` throws when the component has no page file, naming the closest one:

```text
'Users/Indx' was not found in 'ClientApp/pages' ... Did you mean 'Users/Index'?
```

Names match exactly, as the client resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems. Outside Development there is no check and no file access.

`Pages.Extensions` lists the file types: `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.vue` and `.svelte` by default.

## Generated TypeScript

The development startup also writes TypeScript declarations when `o.TypeScript.OutputPath` is set. It only writes the file when the content changed. See [TypeScript types](/docs/typescript).

## What to check before deploying

- `Pages.Directory` can stay configured; it is inactive outside Development.
- DevTools recording is off unless explicitly enabled.
- The generated TypeScript file is committed if the client build type-checks in CI.
- Production logs do not contain the DevTools read API.

<Callout type="tip" title="Pair with the browser extension">
Install the Inertia DevTools extension, open your app in Development, and use the extension's panel. The server entries are correlated by the `X-Inertia-Devtools-Id` header.
</Callout>

---

# Migrating from other adapters

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/migrating

> Map an InertiaCore-style API to Inertia.Net and check the behavior differences.

The API is close to the Laravel adapter's names. The table maps the typical InertiaCore-style API (kapi2289/InertiaCore and its forks). Check names against the version you use.

| Other adapters | Inertia.Net |
|---|---|
| `Inertia.Render("Users/Index", new { users })` | `Render("Users/Index", new InertiaProps { ["users"] = users })`, or a typed props object |
| `return Inertia.Render(...)` in a controller (`Task<IActionResult>`) | `return Render(...)` as `IResult` (MVC executes it) |
| `Inertia.Lazy(() => ...)` / `LazyProp` | `Optional(() => ...)` (never on first load) or `Prop(() => ...)` (lazy, included by default) |
| `Inertia.Defer(...)` / `Inertia.Defer(..., "group")` | `Defer(..., group: "group")` |
| `Inertia.Always(...)` | `Always(...)` |
| `Inertia.Merge(...)` / `DeepMerge` | `Merge(...)`, `DeepMerge(...)`, plus `.Prepend()`, `.MatchOn()` |
| (not supported) | `Once(...)`, `Scroll(...)`, `.Rescue()`, `.Parallel()`, `.Cache(key, duration)` |
| `Inertia.Share("key", value)` | `o.Share("key", value)`, `o.Share("key", ctx => ...)`, or `ctx.Inertia().Share(...)` |
| `Inertia.Location(url)` | `Location(url)` |
| `Inertia.Back()` | `Back()` / `Back(fallback)` |
| `Inertia.ClearHistory()`, `Inertia.EncryptHistory()` | `ctx.Inertia().ClearHistory()`, `ctx.Inertia().EncryptHistory()` (per request, no shared state) |
| `Inertia.Html(...)` / `Inertia.Head` in `_Layout.cshtml` | `app.html` with `@inertia`, `@inertiaHead`, `@vite(...)`, or the Razor tag helpers |
| Flash via `TempData` or session | `ctx.Inertia().Flash(...)`, `Back().WithFlash(...)` (encrypted cookie by default) |
| `ModelState` errors in session | MVC: `AddInertiaMvc()`; Minimal API: `.WithInertiaValidation()`; FastEndpoints: `c.UseInertia()` |
| `Version` option or manifest hashing per request | `o.Version`, `o.VersionResolver`, or the cached manifest hash |
| SSR options (`UseSsr`, `SsrUrl`) | `o.Ssr.Mode`, `o.Ssr.Urls`, `o.Ssr.ExcludePaths`, `Render(...).WithSsr(...)` |

## Behavior differences to check

- **v3 only.** There is no v2 client support. Upgrade the client packages to v3. The first page is the `<script data-page="app">` element, not a `data-page` attribute on the root div.
- **Props are resolved without reflection.** Anonymous types need reflection-enabled serialization, and AOT apps register a `JsonSerializerContext`.
- **HTTP JSON options.** Props serialize with the HTTP JSON options (camelCase by default), not Newtonsoft.
- **Version check before the handler.** A stale client gets a `409` before your endpoint runs.
- **State is an encrypted cookie by default.** Flash, errors and history flags use it unless you opt into the session store.

## Upgrading Inertia.Net

Package upgrade notes live in the repository:

- [1.4 upgrade notes](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/docs/migrating-to-1.4.md)
- [1.3 upgrade notes](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/docs/migrating-to-1.3.md)
- [1.1 upgrade notes](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/docs/migrating-to-1.1.md)

<Callout type="tip" title="Use the same version">
Update all Inertia.Net packages together. Mixing 1.5 with 1.4 packages can compile but produce different protocol output.
</Callout>

---

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/troubleshooting

> Common errors, their causes, and how to fix them.

## `Inertia.Render(...)` does not compile

`'Inertia' is a namespace`. Call `Render(...)` unqualified. The namespace `Inertia.Net` shadows the class name outside the `Inertia.Net` namespace.

The global usings come from the package's `buildTransitive` props and need `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`. Without implicit usings, or with `InertiaNetImplicitUsings` set to `false`, add `using static Inertia.Net.Inertia;`.

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem title="Generated code fails with 'Inertia' is a type">
    Inside a namespace that starts with `Inertia.Net.`, the name `Inertia` binds to the `Inertia.Net.Inertia` class. Source generators that emit non-`global::` names starting with `Inertia` then break. Do not put your app's code under an `Inertia.Net.*` namespace.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite manifest not found. Looked in: ...">
    Run `npm run build`, or start the dev server so the hot file exists in Development, or set `o.Vite.ManifestPath` / `o.Vite.BuildDirectory`. Check that Vite writes `.vite/manifest.json` (`build.manifest: true`, Vite 5 and later) to `wwwroot/build`, and that the build output is part of what you deploy.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite entry '...' was not found in the manifest">
    The `@vite("...")` argument must equal the manifest key, which is the path relative to the Vite root. The error lists the available entries.
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

## Form submissions fail with 419

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` rejected a request without a valid `X-XSRF-TOKEN`. Check that:

- the page was loaded through the middleware (it sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie);
- the cookie reaches the browser (`Secure` on plain HTTP is dropped; see [Deploying](/docs/deploying));
- all instances share the Data Protection key ring;
- `UseAuthentication()` runs before it.

A sign-in or sign-out changes the token: reload the page, or return `Back()` from `OnRejected`. Exempt webhooks and token-authenticated APIs with `.DisableAntiforgery()` or `ShouldValidate`.

## The Inertia page component was not found

`o.Pages.Directory` is set and the component passed to `Render(...)` has no page file there. Names match exactly, as the client's page resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems; the message suggests the closest page. Fix the name, or check `Pages.Extensions` when your pages use another extension. The check never runs outside Development.

## A redirect to another site turns into a 409

That is `ConvertExternalRedirects` (on by default): an Inertia request cannot follow a redirect to another origin, so it gets `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` and the client does a full visit.

If it happens for your own host, the app is behind a proxy that does not forward the scheme (see [Deploying](/docs/deploying)), or use relative redirects. `o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false` disables the conversion.

## The root view resolves outside the content root

`RootView` and `WithRootView(...)` take a path relative to the content root; absolute paths and `..` are refused. Never derive them from request data.

## The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409

A `409` means the asset version differs between the client and the server. A loop means it never converges: usually the version changes on every request (a `VersionResolver` that returns a new value each time, or a manifest regenerated by a file watcher), or different instances behind a load balancer serve different builds. Use a stable version string.

In Development the manifest hash changes after each `vite build`, which is expected once.

## The dev server tags do not appear

The hot file is read only when `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`. Check that `wwwroot/hot` exists and contains `http://localhost:5173`, or set `o.Vite.DevServerUrl`. Remember `base: '/'` for the dev server in `vite.config`.

## The root template was not found, or @inertia is missing

`RootView` is relative to the **content root**. Copy `app.html` to the output and publish directories (`CopyToOutputDirectory`, `CopyToPublishDirectory`). The template must contain `@inertia`.

## Flash data or errors disappear

The state cookie is limited to about 4 KB by browsers. Flash less data, or use `o.State.UseSession()`. If the app runs on several instances, share Data Protection keys.

If the cookie is never sent back, check the cookie `Secure` flag on HTTP behind a proxy that does not forward `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

## Validation errors do not show up (Minimal API)

Use `.WithInertiaValidation()` on the endpoint. Without it, the built-in `AddValidation()` filter returns a `400` problem details that the Inertia client cannot use. Make sure the model types are `public`.

## Validation keys do not match my field names

Keys go through the JSON naming policy per segment (`Address.Street` becomes `address.street`). In MVC the policy is the one in the MVC `JsonOptions`. The page itself is written with the HTTP `JsonOptions`: keep both policies aligned.

## InertiaProp values can only be serialized by Inertia.Net

An `InertiaProp` ended up somewhere Inertia.Net does not walk: a `Flash(...)` value, a read-only dictionary type that does not implement `IDictionary`, or a type with a custom converter.

Lists, typed dictionaries (`Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` with any key type), `object` members and `IDictionary<string, object?>` are walked. Put props in `InertiaProps`, or declare the member as `InertiaProp` (or `object`) on the typed page object.

## Native AOT: JsonTypeInfo metadata was not provided

Add the type to your `JsonSerializerContext` and chain it with `ConfigureHttpJsonOptions`. Setting `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` in regular builds finds these early. See [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot).

## SSR does not run and there is no error

SSR falls back to client rendering on any failure. Look for the warnings `Inertia SSR failed (...)` and `Inertia SSR skipped (...)`. The first includes the server's hint.

Check `o.Ssr.Mode`, `Urls`, that the Node server is running (`GET /health`; with `UseNodeProcess()` look for `Inertia.Net.Ssr` log lines), that `BundlePath` points at the built file, that the path is not in `ExcludePaths`, and that the page is under `MaxPageBytes`.

Set `Mode = SsrMode.Required` in Development to surface the failure.

## SSR skipped (circuit-open) or (overloaded)

- `circuit-open`: the server failed `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` times in a row and is skipped for `BreakDuration`; the earlier `Inertia SSR failed` warnings say why.
- `overloaded`: more renders arrived than `Concurrency.MaxActive` plus `MaxQueued`, or one waited longer than `QueueTimeout`. Add servers or instances, or raise the limits if the server has headroom.

## Several managed instances never become healthy

Every instance must listen on its own port: the SSR entry has to read `process.env.INERTIA_SSR_PORT`. A bundle built only by `@inertiajs/vite` listens on its baked-in port.

## The SSR output is not hydrated

Use the hydrating client entry shown in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering) and build both bundles from the same sources. The SSR body is marked `data-server-rendered="true"`.

## Does it work behind a path base?

Yes. The page `url` keeps the path base, the Vite URLs include it, and `Back()` works.

## Can I use Newtonsoft.Json?

No. Props use System.Text.Json with the HTTP JSON options.

## Can I mix Razor Pages or views with Inertia pages?

Yes. Inertia handles only the endpoints that return `Render(...)`. The middleware leaves other responses alone, apart from `Vary: X-Inertia`.

---

# Build a todo app

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.yebi.africa/docs/forget-me-not

> Build a complete Inertia.Net todo app with session login, public lists, paginated loading, reminders and SSR.

ForgetMeNot is a small todo app, but it uses the same pieces as a real product: sign-in, private data, a public share page, a list that loads as you scroll, and reminders that run in the background. You will start from the official `Inertia.Net.Templates` template, then add each feature one small step at a time.

<Callout type="info" title="What you need">
- .NET 10 SDK
- Bun 1.4 or newer
- A code editor
- A terminal

No database server is required. ForgetMeNot uses SQLite, and the template already gives you a working React app.
</Callout>

This guide is for someone who has not built an Inertia app before. Run the commands, look at the checkpoints, and only move on when the app behaves the way the checkpoint says.

## What you are building

<Cards>
  <Card title="Sign in with sessions" icon="shield">Register, sign in, sign out and keep flash messages in the same session.</Card>
  <Card title="Private todo lists" icon="book">Create lists, add items, mark them done and set due dates.</Card>
  <Card title="Public share pages" icon="sparkles">Share an unguessable URL that opens without an account.</Card>
  <Card title="Virtual loading" icon="code">Load todo items in pages with `Scroll` and `InfiniteScroll`.</Card>
  <Card title="Reminders" icon="gauge">Set a reminder time and let a background worker send it once.</Card>
  <Card title="Pretty UI" icon="blocks">Use Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components instead of inline styles.</Card>
</Cards>

## 1. Start from the template

Install the templates once, then create the app:

```sh
dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates::1.5.3
dotnet new inertia -n ForgetMeNot --framework react
cd ForgetMeNot
bun install
```

Start the two development processes. Keep both terminals open:

```sh
# terminal 1
bun run dev

# terminal 2
dotnet watch
```

Open `http://localhost:5180`. You should see the template home page and a working Todos page. Click around before changing anything.

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
If the app does not load, run `dotnet new inertia --help` and confirm the template version. The frontend must be started before `dotnet watch` reads the Vite hot file, but a refresh is enough if you started them in the other order.
</Callout>

Open these files. You do not need to understand all of them yet:

```text
Program.cs
app.html
ClientApp/app.tsx
ClientApp/Layout.tsx
ClientApp/pages/Home.tsx
ClientApp/pages/Todos/Index.tsx
```

The template already has Inertia, Vite, a deferred prop, a form and validation. We are going to grow it into a full app.

## 2. Make it look good with shadcn/ui

The template uses a tiny inline-style layout. Replace it with Tailwind and shadcn/ui.

Install the packages:

```sh
bun add -d tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
bun add class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react
```

Update `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
import path from 'node:path'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'
// ...your existing imports

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), inertia(), hotFile()],
  resolve: {
    alias: { '@': path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'ClientApp') },
  },
  // ...the rest stays the same
})
```

Add these two properties inside `compilerOptions` in `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./ClientApp/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Create `ClientApp/app.css` and import it from `ClientApp/app.tsx`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

```tsx
// ClientApp/app.tsx
import './app.css'
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'

createInertiaApp()
```

Now initialize shadcn/ui from the project directory:

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn@latest init
```

Accept the defaults. When it asks for the CSS file, choose `ClientApp/app.css`; when it asks for the import alias, use `@/`. Then add the components we need:

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn@latest add button card input label badge checkbox separator
```

<Callout type="tip" title="Checkpoint">
`ClientApp/components/ui/` should now contain `button.tsx`, `card.tsx`, `input.tsx` and the other components. If the CLI asks a question you do not understand, choose the default; you can always rerun it.
</Callout>

Replace `ClientApp/Layout.tsx` with the shared shell:

```tsx
import { Link, usePage } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { LogOut, NotebookPen, UserRound } from 'lucide-react'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { props, flash } = usePage()

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-background text-foreground">
      <header className="border-b">
        <div className="mx-auto flex h-16 max-w-5xl items-center gap-4 px-4">
          <Link href="/" className="flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold">
            <NotebookPen className="size-5 text-primary" />
            ForgetMeNot
          </Link>

          <nav className="ml-auto flex items-center gap-2">
            {props.auth ? (
              <>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm"><Link href="/todos">My lists</Link></Button>
                <span className="hidden items-center gap-1 text-sm text-muted-foreground sm:flex">
                  <UserRound className="size-4" /> {props.auth.displayName}
                </span>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm">
                  <Link href="/logout" method="post" as="button"><LogOut className="size-4" /> Sign out</Link>
                </Button>
              </>
            ) : (
              <>
                <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm"><Link href="/login">Sign in</Link></Button>
                <Button asChild size="sm"><Link href="/register">Create account</Link></Button>
              </>
            )}
          </nav>
        </div>
      </header>

      {flash.success && (
        <div className="border-b bg-emerald-50 px-4 py-2 text-center text-sm text-emerald-800 dark:bg-emerald-950/40 dark:text-emerald-200">
          {flash.success}
        </div>
      )}

      <main className="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-4 py-10">{children}</main>
    </div>
  )
}
```

And replace the template home page with a friendly landing page:

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Home.tsx
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { ArrowRight, CheckCircle2 } from 'lucide-react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card'
import Layout from '../Layout'

export default function Home() {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <section className="mx-auto max-w-3xl py-16 text-center">
        <Badge variant="secondary">Inertia.Net sample</Badge>
        <h1 className="mt-6 text-balance text-5xl font-semibold tracking-tight">
          Remember everything. Share what matters.
        </h1>
        <p className="mx-auto mt-4 max-w-xl text-lg text-muted-foreground">
          Private lists, public links, due dates and reminders — built with ASP.NET Core and Inertia.
        </p>
        <div className="mt-8 flex justify-center gap-3">
          <Button asChild size="lg"><Link href="/register">Create an account <ArrowRight className="size-4" /></Link></Button>
          <Button asChild size="lg" variant="outline"><Link href="/login">Sign in</Link></Button>
        </div>
      </section>

      <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
        {['Private by default', 'One public link', 'Reminders that fire once'].map((text) => (
          <Card key={text}>
            <CardContent className="flex items-center gap-2 p-5 text-sm">
```
